title: Say Less Than Necessary
summary: Speaking less makes you appear more mysterious, intriguing, and powerful. By saying less, you conceal your intentions, reduce your vulnerability, and prevent others from easily deceiving you. Silence prompts others to fill the void, yielding valuable information, while short, enigmatic sentences keep you in control.
example: Louis XIV, who spoke very few words like 'I am state' and 'I shall see' to keep his plans hidden.
Kissinger, who used the single sentence 'Is this best you can do' to psychologically get what he wanted.
A Russian rebellion case where speaking less saved lives.
reversal: Being too silent can arouse suspicion and shift blame to you, as it suggests you are hiding something.
Speaking more can sometimes act as a smokescreen of words, making you appear foolish but effectively concealing your true intentions.
